note: Summaries drafted by a language model from PSI record text. Quotes are kept only if found verbatim in the record.

PSI-10.summary: Burned gas flames on a spherical burner to find when soot starts to form, across flow, dilution and pressure.
PSI-10.relevance: Background science: soot limits feed combustion models. Not a material test.
quotes: Obtain soot-inception limits of quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames

PSI-20.summary: Used a flat gas burner to imitate burning solids and liquids in still air, at atmospheres NASA considers for crewed missions.
PSI-20.relevance: Shows a material can keep burning with no air flow, so stopping ventilation is not enough.
quotes: observed in microgravity despite the absence of air flow

PSI-21.summary: Studied weak and sooty gas flames in a stream of air to test computer models at the extremes of fuel dilution.
PSI-21.relevance: Background science: better flame and soot models.
quotes: Characterize the behavior of weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene

PSI-22.summary: Applied electric fields to small gas flames to see how the field changes their shape, soot and stability.
PSI-22.relevance: Background science. The challenge notes the electric field was used to mimic partial gravity.
quotes: investigates how electric fields influence the behavior of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity

PSI-23.summary: Created spherical gas flames around a porous burner to test models of flame structure and extinction.
PSI-23.relevance: Background science: how simple flames behave near their limits.
quotes: a spherical, one-dimensional stabilized flame

PSI-25.summary: Burned plastic sheets, rods and fabric in a small wind tunnel on the ISS, varying air speed and oxygen.
PSI-25.relevance: Direct evidence on how cabin materials ignite, spread flame and go out in microgravity.
quotes: Study the ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity

PSI-26.summary: Burned fabric, plastic spheres and candles on the ISS, then tried to put the flames out with an inert gas.
PSI-26.relevance: Tests whether the Earth screening test for materials holds in space, and how to extinguish.
quotes: actual material flammability in microgravity

PSI-39.summary: Burned droplets of dodecane fuel at pressures from 0.25 to 5 atm to study cool flames.
PSI-39.relevance: Background science on cool flames, which keep reacting without a visible flame.
quotes: Analyze the effects of helium dilution on cool flame behavior

PSI-47.summary: Checked that a modified particle counter works in microgravity before using it to measure smoke.
PSI-47.relevance: Supports reliable smoke detection on long missions.
quotes: Demonstrate the Functionality of the Modified TSI P-Trak in Microgravity

PSI-60.summary: Reanalyzed more than 1,600 SPICE flame photos to map soot temperature and amount.
PSI-60.relevance: Background science on soot in microgravity flames.
quotes: By analyzing over 1600 raw DSLR images

PSI-62.summary: Built computer models of flames spreading along solids in microgravity, checked against BASS geometries.
PSI-62.relevance: Aims at tools to screen the flammability of new materials.
quotes: predictive tools for screening new materials

PSI-68.summary: Burned droplets of several fuels and mixtures at 0.5 to 3 atm and different oxygen levels.
PSI-68.relevance: Extends FLEX to more fuels. Benchmark data for combustion models.
quotes: varied in pressure between 0.5 atm to 3.0 atm

PSI-69.summary: Burned large fuel droplets while adding gases such as CO2 or helium, to find when the flame goes out.
PSI-69.relevance: Measures how well gas suppressants work in microgravity.
quotes: measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6

PSI-98.summary: Lit a large sheet of cotton-fiberglass fabric inside an uncrewed cargo ship after it left the ISS.
PSI-98.relevance: A first look at how fast a large fire grows in low gravity.
quotes: determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity

PSI-99.summary: Burned nine smaller samples, including silicone, fabric and plastic, inside an uncrewed cargo ship.
PSI-99.relevance: Compares flammability limits in low gravity with NASA's ground screening test.
quotes: investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in

PSI-100.summary: Repeated the large fabric burn of Saffire-I with faster air: 30 cm/s instead of 20.
PSI-100.relevance: Shows how air speed changes the growth of a large fire.
quotes: the experiments were conducted at a flow velocity of 30 cm/s compared to 20 cm/s during Saffire I

PSI-101.summary: Overheated spacecraft materials and measured the smoke particles, with new instruments and a new foam sample.
PSI-101.relevance: Data to design smoke detectors that work in microgravity.
quotes: quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity

PSI-102.summary: Overheated spacecraft materials on the ISS and measured the size of the smoke particles.
PSI-102.relevance: Smoke differs in microgravity, so detectors must be tuned for it.
quotes: quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity

PSI-106.summary: Studied small gas flames that lift off the burner, to learn what keeps a flame anchored.
quotes: better understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity

PSI-107.summary: Burned gas jets in a stream of air to find the point where a flame starts to smoke.
PSI-107.relevance: Background science on soot and smoke production.
quotes: Identify the laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames

PSI-115.summary: Simulated how smoke particles grow in microgravity and in Earth gravity, using the SAME setup.
PSI-115.relevance: Explains why smoke differs in space, which matters for detectors.
quotes: quantify the differences between microgravity and Earth gravity smoke

PSI-117.summary: Simulated droplet cool flames from FLEX to see how heating and drift change their fate.
PSI-117.relevance: Could improve fire-safety models of cool flames.
quotes: Potential to improve spacecraft fire-safety modeling

PSI-142.summary: Used FLEX data, simulations and lab flames to map the limits of cool flames.
PSI-142.relevance: Links the extinction limits of hot flames and cool flames.
quotes: Bridge the knowledge gap between the flammability limits and extinction limits of hot flames and cool flames

PSI-159.summary: Burned light hydrocarbon gases on a spherical burner to find when cool flames appear.
PSI-159.relevance: Holds the highest-oxygen tests in the archive, up to 85%.
quotes: Determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur
